closure.summary: Closure audit of 23 findings from the 2026-07-25 (R1) and 2026-07-26 (R2) reviews against the current draft (index.md, 1,842 lines). Tally: 2 fixed (R1-S03 open-question triage; R2-S02 technical descriptions), 20 partial, 1 open (R2-F02 alt texts). The revision did real work: a statistic-definitions table (L185-211), corrected 5,700-fold scale and 36/35/34/38 counts, a fully specified perturbation estimand (L1099-1126), a defined boundary-shift metric and 'WikiText-versus-code fitting condition' scoping (L1231-1247, L1281-1287), unigram-frequency validation of the prior axis (L604-616), a 'What pre-registered means here' section (L1463-1480), primary-source references for Gemma/WikiText/HSIC/kernel alignment, and hedged key_result wording on probe dependence (L26-30). What is still not closed, and why it matters most: (1) Vocabulary-size causation survives on secondary summary surfaces: the lesson panel (L801-804 'vocabulary size silently sets the floor and a big vocabulary buries the answer'), the shared-contact-sheet caption (L421 'was, in large part, a vocabulary-size effect'), the Gemma-zeros warning panel (L322-325), and the front-matter summary (L8 'Vocabulary crowding is our leading explanation'), which directly contradicts the body's 'Crowding is out' (L739) and open question 5 (L1392-1395). (2) The fixed-vs-fitted fix introduced a new defect: the definitions table (L201-203) and the figure caption/alt (L331-336) still assert fitted_sep >= mid_sep always, while the correction paragraph (L338-349) says 5 of 36 violate it; the five values quoted there are the shared-probe values from atlas_out/shared_summary.csv, not the own-vocabulary summary.csv the paragraph names and the figure receipt hashes (own-vocab summary.csv has a different violator set: gpt2-small, qwen3-1.7b, gemma-4-e2b, qwen2.5-7b-it, gemma-3-27b-it; gpt-oss-20b is not a violator there). These numbers are not in provenance.json. (3) Chronology and counts remain stale: 'three pre-registered designs across six models' (L947), 'Five designs, eleven models' (L1067, L1365, L1550) against 'twelve models' for Test B alone (L1035; union across the five designs is now 15), 'tried to establish it twice' (L1435), 'two withdrawn claims' (L961) vs 'four' (L1636), a garbled tense patch in the appendix (L1755-1757), and ignition-depth/boundary-plasticity still listed as future probes (L938-942, L1078-1079) though both are reported. No pre-data commit is cited in the note; the ledgers hold them (09e5bf7, 4b4f7d5, 1d9bd6d, e09bb2e, 98b1503, 8705791, 86aa050, 3e10ff9). (4) Mechanism language persists: 'tuning a model to answer rewrites its early layers' (L570), 'pulls the early layers' readout into agreement with the late layers'' (L558, L565-567), 'already settled (it is the model)' (L449, contradicting the scope caveat at L438-441), and 'restores structure' in the claims matrix (L1548). (5) Perturbation: the body correctly separates bf16 inference from float32 point estimates (L1112-1119), but the claims matrix re-attaches 'prompt-level bootstraps for #14' to the float32 ratios (L1551, L1563), and the note does not disclose that qwen3.5-0.8b's C = 0.045 is a bf16 value while the other two are float32 (geometry_causality/results.md L300-304). (6) Inline alt texts were not touched: pt-vs-it says 'Seven' curves (L833) while its receipt says eight; the corpus alt implies all models move (L1226) while its receipt says two of three; the contact-sheet alt names no probe (L295). (7) References: the PrimeIntellect 33B/950B ecosystem claim is retained uncited (L85-87, L1511-1512); the body still says Gao et al. 'introduced' the participation ratio (L354) while the reference entry disclaims exactly that (L1795-1797); the community explorer and own release are not revision-pinned; the CKA panel still says CKA is invariant to 'the transformations a network can apply without changing its computation' (L163-164). Em-dash check: zero occurrences.

items.title: Conflicting scales, counts, and statistic identities
items.evidence: Fixed elements: L8 'a 5,700-fold scale span' and L289-290 'a 5,700-fold range of parameters, from a 70M Pythia to the 0.4T Qwen'; definitions table L192-199 ('mid_sep (fixed)', 'fitted_sep', 'own-vocabulary', 'shared-probe', 'public fit', 'independent fit'); L209-211 '36 lenses in the atlas, 35 with a computable readout covariance, 34 with both ..., 38 tokenizers'; L204-207 reconciles qwen3-4b ('a low-separation model on the shared probe and sits in a higher-separation family range on own-vocabulary'); '.472' and '.202' no longer appear anywhere in the note; L765 'gpt-oss-20b is by far the most concentrated model (35% ...)' is now the only concentration superlative. Still conflicting: L201-203 'A fitted_sep is always at least as large as the mid_sep on the same map' versus L338-349 'the guarantee does not, and our own released summary.csv disproves it ... It happens in 5 of our 36 models: gemma-4-e2b (mid_sep +0.081, fitted -0.018), qwen3-1.7b (+0.082, +0.007), qwen2.5-7b-it (+0.014, +0.002), gpt2-small (+0.015, +0.003), gpt-oss-20b (+0.057, +0.051)'. Those five values match experiments/jspace_atlas/atlas_out/shared_summary.csv (shared probe), not summary.csv (own vocabulary), which is the file the paragraph names and the file zoo-mid-vs-fitted.receipt.json hashes; own-vocab summary.csv (pinned de50888 and local) has violators gpt2-small (0.015/0.0014), qwen3-1.7b (0.0758/0.0414), gemma-4-e2b (0.0468/-0.0109), qwen2.5-7b-it (0.0029/0.002), gemma-3-27b-it (0.009/-0.0024), and gpt-oss-20b is NOT a violator there (0.0756/0.0921). None of the five quoted values is in provenance.json.
items.remaining: Reconcile L201-203 with L338-349 (drop the 'always' guarantee from the table). Restate the correction on the probe it was computed on and cite shared_summary.csv (or recompute on summary.csv and list gemma-3-27b-it instead of gpt-oss-20b); add the values to provenance.json. Fix L327-329 'the fixed-thirds mid_sep we released ... is deliberately conservative, and the whole zoo confirms it' and the caption/alt at L331-336, which still assert the ordering the correction retracts.

items.title: Vocabulary-size mechanism is not established
items.evidence: Fixed: key_result L26-30 'Note we do not establish vocabulary size as the cause: the two probes differ in which tokens they contain ... a shared probe, which removes the token-set confound but does not by itself equalise model-specific baselines'; L372-374 'Every probe here contains the same 4,096 rows, so what differs across models is which tokens are sampled ... not how many rows there are'; L387-391 'This equalises which tokens are compared across models. It does not by itself equalise the null floor'; L380-385 per-checkpoint caveat (Qwen3.5 248,320 vs Gemma 256k/262k); L897-898 '(crowding is the natural explanation, but this comparison does not isolate it)'. Still asserting vocabulary size as cause: summary L8 'Vocabulary crowding is our leading explanation but is not isolated by this comparison'; lesson panel L801-804 'It is the wrong question across models, because vocabulary size silently sets the floor and a big vocabulary buries the answer'; L421 'The apparent family split of the own-vocabulary grid was, in large part, a vocabulary-size effect'; L322-325 'exactly the wrong probe for a family with an unusually large vocabulary'. Contradiction: L739 'Crowding is out' and L1392-1395 'every tidy explanation we tested (vocabulary crowding ...) failed' versus the summary's 'leading explanation'.
items.remaining: Rewrite the lesson panel (L801-808), the zoo-contact-shared caption (L421), the Gemma-zeros warning (L322-325) and the summary sentence (L8) to say probe-set dependence, not vocabulary size or crowding; resolve the summary/body contradiction on crowding (either it is the leading hypothesis or it is out).

items.title: Geometry, model mechanism, and metric behavior are conflated
items.evidence: Fixed: L61-66 'readout-geometry regime ... Whether that means the network computes similarly at those depths is a further claim the instrument does not settle'; L248-250 null bounded to 'this random-transport baseline'; L546-547 '(They are not "the same weights": instruct tuning changes the weights ...)'; L780-783 'strongest measured correlate, and the one we can show actually does the masking in this statistic ... a demonstration about the measurement, not about restoring the network's computation'; L789-790 'the ablation is an operation on the statistic, not an intervention on the network'; L604-616 actual unigram-frequency validation (-0.591 with log frequency). Not replaced: L449 'The model-versus-fit question is already settled (it is the model)'; L570 'tuning a model to answer rewrites its early layers to read out what its late layers already do'; L558 'instruct tuning pulls the output-facing geometry toward a common answer-producing direction'; L565-567 'it pulls the early layers' readout into agreement with the late layers' answer-producing geometry, extending the invariant readout backward'; L1548 claims matrix 'Ablating top directions restores structure'; L258-259 'Whatever phase organization appears in the real atlas was put there by the fitted Jacobians'; L229-230 'late-stack blocks where computation turns toward committing outputs'; 'phases' on summary surfaces L7, L19.
items.remaining: Replace 'settled' at L449 (it contradicts the scope caveat at L438-441), 'rewrites'/'pulls' at L558, L565-570, L578, and 'restores' at L1548 with associational/geometric wording; bound L229-230 and L258-259 to readout geometry.

items.title: Perturbation result lacks a publication-grade estimand
items.evidence: Fixed: L1099-1110 'At each lens layer we add a fixed-norm vector to the residual stream at all positions, and read the KL divergence ... over 200 held-out WikiText passages ... identical vector norm, verified to within 10^-6 relative, and epsilon = 0 reproduces the clean logits exactly ... The random floor is 8 independent unit vectors per layer, averaged. The reported ratio is exp(median_l log(KL_lens / mean KL_random)) ... 2,000-resample bootstrap over prompts; the per-model 95% intervals on the log ratio exclude zero: gpt2-small [+1.22, +1.38], gemma-3-270m [+2.00, +2.18], qwen3.5-0.8b [+1.76, +2.22]' (matches geometry_causality/results.md L18-22); L1121-1126 comparator defined as 'the unit-normalised gradient of the clean top-1 token's log-probability' and 'We had labelled it a ceiling; that was wrong'; L1118-1119 conditioning on the eight realised random directions stated. Not done: heading L1083 'The lens directions are real: 7.5x to 9.1x over an equal-norm random direction' still uses the 'real' framing the review asked to drop; L1133-1135 'picks directions that move the output several times more than chance' is fine, but L1128 'Confirmed in all three families' leads with the float32 magnitudes that carry no interval.
items.remaining: Retitle L1083 to the bounded statement ('beat an equal-norm random direction by 7.5x to 9.1x'); see R2-B03 for the interval attachment residual.

items.evidence: Fixed: L309-310 'Both statements are descriptive of this collection of lenses on their own vocabularies'; L1189-1190 'This is a census of an opportunistically assembled collection, not a random sample of models, so read it as a striking association within these 36 rather than a law about training families'; L1564-1566 'Rows marked census are descriptive of the 36-lens collection and are not population inference, because the collection is a convenience sample with family clustering'; 'decides' no longer appears. Remaining: L317 'Scale alone plainly does not set the band'; L541-542 'instruct tuning flattens the readout, in every family, monotonically' (only three families have pairs: L555 alt 'across gemma-2, gemma-3 and llama'); L1188 'family membership is by far the strongest predictor'; no family-cluster uncertainty for rho +0.44 (L549) or -0.59 (L752).
items.remaining: Bound L317, L541-542 and L1188 to 'in this collection' / 'in the three families with pairs'; add cluster-aware uncertainty or drop inferential verbs for the zoo correlations.

confirmed.location: summary L8; key_result L26-28; contact-shared caption L421; lesson panel L801-805; L322-325; L739; L1392-1395

confirmed.location: key_result L19-21; atlas figure-note L216-222; L224-233; control section L238-262; L873-887; Discussion L1447-1452; claims row 1
confirmed.problem: The random-J null has no depth ordering, so it cannot distinguish 'three phases' from 'CKA decays smoothly with layer distance'. A distance-only (Toeplitz) model reproduces 89% of off-diagonal variance, 80% of mid_sep (0.275 vs 0.343) and nearly the same fitted anatomy (11,48 vs 13,46). Adjacent-layer CKA is 0.979-1.000 at every interior layer; the 41/42 drop (0.983) is no sharper than 49/50; only layers 55-57 turn fast. Localised extra rotation near 11-13 and 41-45 exists, so 'regimes' is defensible; 'clean', 'sharp', 'brief fast turns' are not.
confirmed.fix: Add the distance-only null beside the random one (its mid_sep, fitted segmentation, residual map C - C_dist as a third panel) and rewrite the boundary prose to what adjacent-layer CKA shows. CPU, minutes.
